title: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body

learn.hook: Your plate of dal, rice and sabzi is actually a team of tiny helpers. Each one has a job to do in your body!
points: Nutrients are the parts of food our body needs to stay healthy.
Carbohydrates (rice, wheat roti, potato, millets like ragi and bajra) give us energy. Fats (ghee, butter, oil, nuts) give even more energy.
Proteins (dal, rajma, milk, paneer, eggs, fish, soybean) are body-building foods: they help us grow and repair the body.
Vitamins and minerals (fruits, vegetables, milk) protect us from diseases and keep the body working well.
Dietary fibre (roughage) in whole grains, fruits and vegetables helps the body get rid of undigested food. Water helps carry nutrients and remove wastes as sweat and urine.

example.q: Aman plays football for two hours every evening. Which nutrient does he mainly need for energy, and from which food?
steps: Running and kicking use a lot of energy.
Carbohydrates and fats are energy-giving nutrients.
Foods like rice, roti, potato and millets are rich in carbohydrates.
example.answer: Carbohydrates, from foods like rice, roti and millets (fats also give energy).

learn.reallife: In school, with a teacher, a drop of dilute iodine solution on a potato slice turns it blue-black, showing starch (a carbohydrate). Rubbing a groundnut on paper leaves an oily patch that light shines through, showing fat. Never taste or play with lab chemicals.

quiz.q: Which nutrient helps our body grow and repair itself?
quiz.explain: Proteins are called body-building foods because they help in growth and repair.
steps: The question asks which nutrient helps growth and repair.
Proteins are body-building foods: they help us grow and repair the body.
Carbohydrates and fats mainly give energy; fibre helps remove undigested food.
So the answer is proteins.
Answer: Proteins
quiz.mistake: Thinks energy foods are the body-building foods

quiz.q: Which food is rich in carbohydrates?
quiz.explain: Rice contains a lot of starch, which is a carbohydrate.
steps: Carbohydrates are found in rice, roti, potato and millets.
Rice has a lot of starch, which is a carbohydrate.
Paneer and egg white are proteins; ghee is fat.
So rice is rich in carbohydrates.
Answer: Rice
quiz.mistake: Mixes up carbohydrate foods with protein or fat foods

quiz.q: Which food is a good source of protein?
quiz.explain: Pulses like moong dal are rich in protein.
steps: Proteins come from dal, rajma, milk, paneer, eggs, fish and soybean.
Moong dal is a pulse, rich in protein.
Sugar is a carbohydrate; butter is fat; potato is mainly starch.
So moong dal is a good protein source.
Answer: Moong dal
quiz.mistake: Does not know pulses are protein-rich

quiz.q: Which nutrient gives the MOST energy for the same amount of food?
quiz.explain: Fats give more than twice the energy of the same weight of carbohydrates or proteins.
steps: Carbohydrates and fats both give energy.
Fats give even more energy — more than twice as much for the same weight.
Vitamins and water give no energy.
So fats give the most energy.
Answer: Fats
quiz.mistake: Thinks vitamins or proteins are the biggest energy source

quiz.q: What does dietary fibre (roughage) do?
options: Helps the body get rid of undigested food
quiz.explain: Fibre adds bulk and helps undigested food move out of the body, preventing constipation.
steps: Dietary fibre (roughage) is found in whole grains, fruits and vegetables.
It helps the body get rid of undigested food.
It does not give the most energy or build muscles.
So fibre helps the body get rid of undigested food.
Answer: Helps the body get rid of undigested food
quiz.mistake: Thinks fibre is an energy or body-building nutrient

quiz.q: Which test result shows that a food contains starch?
options: It leaves an oily patch on paper
It turns blue-black with dilute iodine solution
quiz.explain: Starch turns blue-black when a drop of dilute iodine solution is added.
steps: Test for starch: add a drop of dilute iodine solution.
Starch turns blue-black.
An oily patch on paper is the test for fat.
So turning blue-black with iodine shows starch.
Answer: It turns blue-black with dilute iodine solution
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the starch test with the fat test

quiz.q: Rubbing a groundnut on paper leaves a patch that light shines through. What does this show?
quiz.explain: An oily patch that lets light through shows that fat is present.
steps: Test for fat: rub the food on paper.
A translucent (light-shining) oily patch shows fat is present.
Starch is tested with iodine, not paper.
So the groundnut has fat.
Answer: The groundnut has fat
quiz.mistake: Thinks the paper test shows starch

quiz.q: Why do we need water even though it gives no energy?
options: It helps carry nutrients and remove wastes
It gives more energy than fat
quiz.explain: Water helps the body absorb nutrients and remove wastes through sweat and urine.
steps: Water gives no energy, but the body still needs it.
Water helps carry nutrients and remove wastes as sweat and urine.
So we need water because it helps carry nutrients and remove wastes.
Answer: It helps carry nutrients and remove wastes
quiz.mistake: Thinks only energy-giving foods are useful

teach.ask: Gappu stares at his plate: 'Why can't I eat only sweets all day? What do different foods do for my body?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Carbs and fats give energy, proteins build the body, vitamins and minerals protect me. Sweets alone can't do all that!
teach.nudge: Which food helps me grow, and which food keeps me from getting sick?

revise.summary: Nutrients are the parts of food our body needs: carbohydrates and fats give energy, proteins build and repair the body, vitamins and minerals protect us, and fibre and water keep the body working well.

learn.hook: A cricket team needs batters, bowlers and a keeper. Your meal also needs a full team of nutrients!
points: A balanced diet has all the nutrients in the right amounts, along with fibre and water.
How much food we need depends on our age, how active we are and our health. A growing child and a farmer need plenty of energy.
Indian meals like dal-chawal with sabzi and curd, or roti with dal and salad, can be nicely balanced.
Millets like ragi, jowar and bajra are nutritious grains. The United Nations named 2023 the International Year of Millets.
Mindful eating means eating slowly, chewing well, stopping when full, eating fresh home-cooked food, eating less junk food and not wasting food.

example.q: Priya's lunch is only puri and aloo sabzi, with a glass of cola. How can she make it balanced?
steps: Puri (fried) and potato give carbohydrates and fat, which are energy.
Missing: protein, enough vitamins and minerals, and fibre. Cola adds lots of sugar.
Add dal or curd for protein, a salad or green vegetable for vitamins and fibre, and drink water instead of cola.
example.answer: Add dal or curd, a green vegetable or salad, and choose water instead of cola.

learn.reallife: Each region of India has its own balanced meals: idli-sambar in the south, dal-baati in Rajasthan, fish-rice in Bengal and makki roti with sarson saag in Punjab.

quiz.q: What is a balanced diet?
options: Food with all nutrients in the right amounts, plus fibre and water
quiz.explain: A balanced diet gives the body everything it needs in the right amounts.
steps: The question asks the meaning of a balanced diet.
A balanced diet has all the nutrients in the right amounts, with fibre and water.
Only proteins, only fruits or eating as much as possible are not balanced.
So it is food with all nutrients in the right amounts, plus fibre and water.
Answer: Food with all nutrients in the right amounts, plus fibre and water
quiz.mistake: Thinks one kind of nutrient is enough

quiz.q: Which meal is the most balanced?
options: Roti, dal, green sabzi, salad and curd
quiz.explain: This meal has carbohydrates (roti), protein (dal, curd), vitamins, minerals and fibre (sabzi, salad).
steps: A balanced meal includes energy food, body-building food, vitamins, minerals and fibre.
Roti (carbohydrate), dal and curd (protein), sabzi and salad (vitamins, minerals, fibre).
Noodles, chips, soft drinks or sweets alone lack many nutrients.
So roti, dal, green sabzi, salad and curd is most balanced.
Answer: Roti, dal, green sabzi, salad and curd
quiz.mistake: Picks a meal that tastes good but lacks nutrients

quiz.q: Which of these is a millet?
quiz.explain: Ragi (finger millet) is a millet. Rice and wheat are other cereals, and potato is a tuber.
steps: Millets are nutritious grains like ragi, jowar and bajra.
Rice and wheat are other cereals; potato is a tuber.
So ragi is a millet.
Answer: Ragi
quiz.mistake: Thinks all grains are millets

quiz.q: Why should we eat junk food only rarely?
options: It is very rich in fibre
It has too much fat, salt or sugar and few useful nutrients
quiz.explain: Junk food fills us up with fat, salt and sugar but lacks proteins, vitamins and fibre.
steps: Mindful eating means eating less junk food.
Junk food has too much fat, salt or sugar.
It has few useful nutrients like proteins, vitamins and fibre.
So eat it rarely because it has too much fat, salt or sugar and few nutrients.
Answer: It has too much fat, salt or sugar and few useful nutrients
quiz.mistake: Thinks tasty food is always nutritious

quiz.q: Which is an example of mindful eating?
options: Eating very fast while watching a screen
Eating slowly and stopping when you feel full
quiz.explain: Paying attention while eating helps digestion and stops overeating.
steps: Mindful eating: eat slowly, chew well, stop when full.
Eating fast at a screen, wasting food or skipping breakfast are not mindful.
So eating slowly and stopping when full is mindful eating.
Answer: Eating slowly and stopping when you feel full
quiz.mistake: Does not know what mindful eating means

quiz.q: Who needs more energy-giving food?
options: A farmer ploughing a field all day
A person sitting still for an hour
quiz.explain: Hard physical work uses more energy, so a farmer working all day needs more energy food.
steps: Food needed depends on age, activity and health.
A farmer ploughing all day does hard physical work and uses lots of energy.
Sleeping or sitting still uses much less.
So the farmer needs more energy-giving food.
Answer: A farmer ploughing a field all day
quiz.mistake: Thinks everyone needs the same amount of food

quiz.q: The International Year of Millets was in which year?
quiz.explain: The United Nations named 2023 the International Year of Millets.
steps: Millets are nutritious grains.
The United Nations named 2023 the International Year of Millets.
So the year was 2023.
Answer: 2023
quiz.mistake: Confuses the year

quiz.q: Which habit helps reduce food waste?
options: Taking a big helping and leaving most of it
Cooking food and throwing it away
Taking only as much food as you can eat
quiz.explain: Taking small helpings and asking for more if needed means less food is thrown away.
steps: Mindful eating includes not wasting food.
Taking only as much as you can eat leaves nothing to throw away.
Taking big helpings and leaving most of it wastes food.
So take only as much food as you can eat.
Answer: Taking only as much food as you can eat
quiz.mistake: Does not connect serving size with waste

teach.ask: Gappu's tummy rumbles: 'I eat only grains all day. My friend says I need a balanced diet. What does that mean?'
teach.praise: Tweet! A balanced diet has all the nutrients in the right amounts, plus fibre and water. I'll add some greens to my grains!
teach.nudge: Do I need just one kind of nutrient, or many? And how much of each?

revise.summary: A balanced diet has all the nutrients in the right amounts, with fibre and water. Mindful eating means eating slowly, stopping when full, eating fresh food, less junk food and not wasting food.
focus: What makes a meal balanced, using Indian meals
How age, activity and health change food needs
Millets and the International Year of Millets (2023)
Habits of mindful eating and reducing food waste
remember: Balanced diet = all nutrients in the right amounts + fibre + water
Millets: ragi, jowar, bajra; 2023 = International Year of Millets
Mindful eating: eat slowly, chew well, stop when full, waste less
traps: Don't think eating as much as possible is a balanced diet.
Junk food is not useful food: it has too much fat, salt or sugar and few nutrients.
Rice and wheat are cereals but not millets.

learn.hook: If your body misses one tiny vitamin for a long time, it can show signs like weak bones or bleeding gums. Good food fixes it!
points: A deficiency disease happens when the body does not get enough of a nutrient for a long time.
Vitamin A: poor eyesight, especially night blindness (eat carrots, papaya, mango, milk). Vitamin B1: beriberi, weak muscles (eat whole grains, pulses).
Vitamin C: scurvy, bleeding gums (eat amla, guava, oranges, lemons). Vitamin D: rickets, soft and bent bones (sunlight, milk, eggs, fish).
Calcium: weak bones and teeth (milk, curd, ragi). Iodine: goitre, a swelling in the neck (iodised salt). Iron: anaemia, feeling tired and weak (green leafy vegetables, pulses).
Deficiency diseases can be prevented by eating a balanced diet.

example.q: Raju's gums bleed often. His doctor says he needs more of a certain vitamin. Which vitamin, and what should he eat?
steps: Bleeding gums are a sign of scurvy.
Scurvy is caused by a lack of vitamin C.
Vitamin C is found in citrus fruits, amla and guava.
example.answer: Vitamin C; he should eat amla, guava, oranges or lemons.

learn.reallife: Common table salt in India is often iodised to prevent goitre, and many children get vitamin D by playing in the morning sunshine.

games.title: Match the deficiency to the disease

items.q: Bleeding gums: which vitamin is lacking?
Night blindness: which vitamin is lacking?
Feeling tired due to anaemia: which mineral is lacking?
Mineral for strong bones and teeth?

quiz.q: What causes a deficiency disease?
options: Lack of a nutrient in the diet for a long time
quiz.explain: Deficiency diseases are caused by not getting enough of a nutrient over a long time, not by germs.
steps: A deficiency disease is caused by lack of a nutrient.
It happens when the body does not get enough for a long time.
It is not caused by germs.
So the cause is lack of a nutrient in the diet for a long time.
Answer: Lack of a nutrient in the diet for a long time
quiz.mistake: Thinks all diseases spread from person to person

quiz.q: Lack of vitamin C causes:
quiz.explain: Scurvy, with bleeding gums, is caused by a lack of vitamin C.
steps: Vitamin C deficiency causes scurvy, with bleeding gums.
Rickets = vitamin D; goitre = iodine; night blindness = vitamin A.
So lack of vitamin C causes scurvy.
Answer: Scurvy
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the vitamins and their diseases

quiz.q: A child with soft, bent bones may have rickets. Which vitamin is lacking?
quiz.explain: Vitamin D helps the body use calcium for strong bones. Its lack causes rickets.
steps: Rickets means soft and bent bones.
It is caused by a lack of vitamin D (from sunlight, milk, eggs, fish).
So the vitamin lacking is vitamin D.
Answer: Vitamin D
quiz.mistake: Mixes up vitamin D with other vitamins

quiz.q: Which disease is caused by a lack of iodine?
quiz.explain: Lack of iodine causes goitre, a swelling of the neck. Iodised salt helps prevent it.
steps: Goitre is a swelling in the neck.
It is caused by a lack of iodine.
Iodised salt helps prevent it.
So lack of iodine causes goitre.
Answer: Goitre
quiz.mistake: Confuses mineral and vitamin deficiencies

quiz.q: Which food is a rich source of vitamin C?
quiz.explain: Amla (Indian gooseberry) is very rich in vitamin C.
steps: Vitamin C sources: amla, guava, oranges, lemons.
Ghee is fat; sugar and white rice are carbohydrates.
So amla is a rich source of vitamin C.
Answer: Amla
quiz.mistake: Picks an energy food instead of a protective food

quiz.q: Night blindness is caused by a lack of:
quiz.explain: Vitamin A keeps our eyes healthy. Its lack causes night blindness.
steps: Night blindness is poor eyesight in dim light.
It is caused by a lack of vitamin A (carrots, papaya, mango, milk).
So the answer is vitamin A.
Answer: Vitamin A
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the vitamin needed for eyes

quiz.q: Meena feels tired and weak all the time, and her doctor says she has anaemia. What should she eat more of?
options: Iron-rich foods like green leafy vegetables
quiz.explain: Anaemia is often caused by a lack of iron. Green leafy vegetables and pulses provide iron.
steps: Anaemia makes a person feel tired and weak.
It is caused by a lack of iron.
Iron comes from green leafy vegetables and pulses.
So she should eat iron-rich foods like green leafy vegetables.
Answer: Iron-rich foods like green leafy vegetables
quiz.mistake: Thinks sugary food will cure tiredness

quiz.q: How can deficiency diseases be prevented?
quiz.explain: A balanced diet supplies all the nutrients, so no deficiency develops.
steps: Deficiency diseases come from missing nutrients.
A balanced diet supplies all nutrients in the right amounts.
So they can be prevented by eating a balanced diet.
Answer: By eating a balanced diet
quiz.mistake: Does not connect a balanced diet with preventing disease

teach.ask: Gappu looks worried: 'My cousin's gums bleed. Is it a germ? How can food make someone sick or well?'
teach.praise: Phew! It's a deficiency, not a germ. Eating a balanced diet with all vitamins and minerals keeps such diseases away!
teach.nudge: But what is missing in the body? And how can we stop it from happening?

revise.summary: A deficiency disease happens when the body lacks a nutrient for a long time, like scurvy (vitamin C), rickets (vitamin D) or goitre (iodine). A balanced diet prevents them.
focus: Matching each deficiency disease to the missing nutrient
remember: Vitamin A → night blindness; Vitamin B1 → beriberi
Vitamin C → scurvy (bleeding gums); Vitamin D → rickets (soft, bent bones)
Iodine → goitre (neck swelling); Iron → anaemia; Calcium → weak bones and teeth
Prevent all of them with a balanced diet
traps: Deficiency diseases are not caused by germs or catching them from friends.
Don't mix up scurvy (vitamin C) and rickets (vitamin D).
Goitre is from lack of iodine, not iron.
